column2: Further forms of nadi: "nadya, nadibhih, nadyai, nadyam, nadishu"; kumari, jrimbhani likewise; shri: "shrih, shriyau, shriyah, shriya" (declension of feminine nouns).
Shriyai, shriye; stri, striyam, strih, striyah, striya, striyai, striyah, strinam, striyam; gramani; dhenu: "dhenvai, dhenave" (declension).
Jambu: "jambuh, jambvau, jambuh, jambunam, phalam"; varshabhu, punarbhu, matri; go: "gauh"; nau (declension examples).
Vach: "vak, vacha, vagbhih, vakshu"; sraj: "sragbhyam, srajoh"; vidvas: "vidvadbhyam, vidvatsu"; bhavati and bhavanti (declension).
Divyanti, bhati, bhanti, tudanti, tudati, rudati, rundhati, devi, grihnati, choryanti (feminine participles).
Drishad: "drishat, drishadbhyam, drishadi"; vishesavidushi, kriti; samit: "samidbhyam, samidhi"; sima: "simni, siman" (declension).
Daman: "damanibhyam"; kakubh: "kakudbhyam"; kimidam: "keyam, abhyam, asu"; gir: "girbhyam, gira, girshu"; subhu, supu, pur: "pura, puri" (declension).

Dyu: "dyaur, dyubhyam, divi, dyushu"; tadrish: "tadrishya, tadrishah, disah; yadrishyam, yadrishi" likewise; suvachas: "suvachobhyam, suvachahsu"; asau: "amum, amu, amuh, amubhih, amuyam, amuyoh" (declension).
Kartri: "karta, kartrina, kartre"; ati, yati, rini; abhi, nyabhi, nini; suvachamsi, suvachamsi, suvakshu (declension of neuter and others).
Yad: "yat, yat, ime, tat karmani, idam, ime, imani"; idrik, tvad, amuni, amuni, amuna, amishu (pronoun and neuter forms).
Aham, avam, vayam, mam, abam, asman, maya kritam — I, we two, we, me, by me; (first-person pronoun declension).
Mad, avabhyam, madasmat; this son is mine, of us two; of us, in us; tvam, yuvam, yuyam — you (singular, dual, plural).
Tvam, yuvam, yushman; tvaya, yushmabhih; tubhyam, yuvabhyam, yushmabhyam; tvat, yuvabhyam, yushmat (second-person declension).
Tava, yuvayoh, yushmakam; tvayi, yushmasu — Bharati (Sarasvati). Here only the indication is given; those ending in vowels and consonants are remembered.
By the eye one takes form; the external one cuts it with a sickle. The dative is declared threefold: instigating (one gives a cow to a Brahmin),
a man gives also to the king, a slave consenting; non-refusing, a good man would give flowers to his master.
The ablative is declared twofold: movable, from a running horse; fallen, immovable, from the village — one comes, that Vaishnava.
The locative is fourfold: pervading — ghee in curd; oil in sesame; for the god, aupashleshika;
a monkey stays in the house, in the tree is called vaishayika; "a fish in water, a lion in the forest" is remembered as samipyaka;
a cowherd settlement lives on the Ganga — aupacharika is of this kind. The third or sixth case is remembered in the non-expressed;
Vishnu is worshipped by people or "to be gone to by him." With the agent and object expressed first, one should bow to Hari;
in the sense of cause the third case: "he lives by food"; "water for the tree"; the fourth in the sense of purpose; the fifth by words with pari, upa, a, mukha;
it has rained around the village; "this god is mighty of old"; "the earlier from the village"; "without Vishnu no liberation, the other is of Hari" (usage examples).
With "prithak," "vina" and the like, the third and fifth cases are possible: "apart from the village, without outing, Shri by Shri's" (usage).
With the so-called karma-pravachaniyas the second case arises by connection: "the warriors after Arjuna"; "around the village" is said.
With namah, svaha, svadha, svasti, vashat and the like, also the fourth: "homage to the god; blessing to you"; and from the sense of an infinitive-noun.
For cooking, to cook; the third case with connection (saha); in the sense of cause, in a blamed limb, and in qualifier:
the father went with his son; "one-eyed in the eye"; "Hari with a mace"; "the servant lives for the purpose"; the seventh in time and state;
to Vishnu bowed there would be liberation; "in spring he went to Hari"; "master of men, among men master; lord of men, lord of the good" (usage).
Witness of men, among men witness; lord of cows, among cows lord; a charioteer among cows; among kings a co-heir here (usage).

He lives for the sake of food — the sixth case; in verbs of remembering with object: "he remembers the protector of his mother"; always in agent and object; "breaker of waters, your work" — the sixth also not in participial endings.
King's man, rajapurusha — the sixth compound; "tree-fruit" likewise; seventh: "aksha-shaunda"; the negative compound "ahita" (examples of compounds).
Karmadharaya sevenfold: neelotpala and the rest; with qualifier first; also with qualified later;
vyakarana-kha-muchi, shita-ushna, dvipada, shubha; with comparison-standard first: "shankhapandara";
with comparison-standard last: "purushavyaghra"; with possibility first: "gunavriddhi" and so on;
guna and vriddhi are to be said; "suhrid, subandhuka"; with determination first; the Bahuvrihi is sevenfold;
two-worded Bahuvrihi: "arudhabhuvana naro"; "this one with worshipped remainder first, bahvanghri (many-footed)" is declared;
these Brahmins are upadasha; with number-last: "dvitra, dvyekatra naro" (examples); with number in both words,
this would be with sa-first: "samulodhrita tarah"; for reciprocity "kesakesi, nakhanakhi" (examples);
direction-marked: "dakshinapurva"; Dvigu is told in two ways: as singular "dvishringa"; "panchamuli" in one way.
Dvandva compound is of two kinds: by mutual joining ("Rudravishnu") and collective ("bheripatahamidrisham").
Avyayibhava is told as twofold: with a noun first: "shakasya matra, shakaprati"; with indeclinable first;

upakumbha, uparathya — it is fourfold by predominance: Tatpurusha with the latter word's meaning chief; Dvandva with both chief; Avyayibhava with the former meaning chief; Bahuvrihi with outside meaning.
In "ini" Daksha (Dakshi), Dasharathi; "Narayana" and the like in "chha"; "Ashvayana" in "phan"; "Gargya" and "Vatsaka" in "yan";
in "dhak" Vainateya and the rest; "Chatakera"; in "drak" "Gaudheraka" — the form Gaudhara; (taddhita examples).
Kshatriya in "gha"; "kulina" in "kha"; "Kairavya" and the like in "nya" are remembered; "murdhanya-mukhya" in "yat"; "sugandhi" is a form.
From tarakadi, "itach": "nabhastarakita" and the rest; with "anang" "kundodhni"; "pushpadhanva", "sudhanvan".
In "chanchup": "vittavanchu" — he has wealth; in "chan": "keshachana", "patarupaka" in "rupa" (taddhita suffixes).
Iyasu: "patiyan"; in "tarap": "akshatara" and the like; "pachatitara", "atatitama";
mridvitama; in "kalpap": "indrakalpa", "arkakalpaka"; "rajadeshiya" in "deshiya", "deshya"; "deshyadirupaka".
Patujatiya in "jatiya"; "janumatra" in "matrach"; "urudvayasa" in "dvayasach"; "urudaghna" in "daghna".
Panchatayah in "tayat"; "dauvarika" in "thak" is declared. The general function is told; and the indeclinable-named taddhita:
from "yasmat," "yatah," "tasil"; "yatra, tatra" in "tral"; "asmin kale: adhuna, idanim, danim";
sarvasmin: sarvada, tasmin kale; "tarhi, harhi" in "rhil"; "tarhi, kasmin cha kalake"; "iha, karhi" (adverbial suffixes).
Yatha, katham in "thal, thamu"; "in the east direction": "purvasyam disi sanchayet" and "astati"; "purvasyah purvadi, gramaniyaka";
purastat sancharet gachchhet; sadyah, tulye ahani is said; in "uti": "parut"; in "purvabde"; "purvatara, parary" (time adverbs).
Aishamas in this year — the form; "samsi" is told; "edyavi, paredyavi" — on the other day is said;
adya — on this day; in "dyu": "purvedyuh", "aidyusi"; "dakshinasyam disi vaset: dakshinat, dakshinadyubhau";
uttarasyam disi vaset, uttarat, uttaradyubhau; "uparivaset": "uparishtat" from "urdhva"; (directional adverbs).
Uttarena told by the father; and "dakshina" in "achi"; "aho": "dakshinahi vaset"; "dvaidha, dvidha" in two kinds and "dha".
Dhyamun: "ekadhyam kuru tvam"; "dvaidham" in "an"; two kinds in "dha" and "achi"; "asusuratara" (adverbial suffix examples).
Particles are said to be taddhita; the taddhita expresses state: "patoh bhavah: patutva, patuta" in "tal" (abstract nouns).
Prithima in "iman" of "prithu"; "saukhya" from "sukha" in "shyan"; "steya" of "stena"; "sakhya" from "sakhi" is said.
Kapeh bhavah: kapeya; "sainya"; "pathya" in "yak"; "ashva", "kaumarka" in "an"; "yauvana"; "acharyaka" in "kan" — thus other taddhitas too.
Svaru, "vajnam", "trapusi", "samasara", "phalgu" are told; "gridhna" in "krana"; "kirach": "mandira", "timira", "tamas".
Ilach: "salila, vari"; "kalyana", "bhandila" are remembered; "budha, vidvan" in "kvasu"; "shivira" is guarded station.
Otu, "vidala" and "tun"; "abhidhana" — Unadi suffixes and the rest: "karna, kami, grihabhuh, vastuh, jaivatrika" are remembered.
Anadvan from "vah" in "vin"; "jiva, arnava, aushadha" in kind; "nau, vahni" in "inin"; "harina, mriga, kami, bhajana".
Kamboja, bhajana, bhanda, saranda the four-footed; "taru, eranda, sanghata, varuda, sama, nirbhara";
sphara, prabhuta in the "na" ending; "chiravalkala"; "katara, bhiru"; "ugra" but "prachanda"; "javasa, trina";
jagat and "bhurloka"; "krishanu, jyotih, arkaka"; "barbara, kutila, dhurta"; "chatvara" is a crossroads;
chivara is a monk's cloth; "aditya" and "mitra" are said; "putra, sunu, pita, tata, pridaku, vyaghra, vrishchika; garta, avata, bharata, nata" and other Unadi words.
Krid, Vrin, Grahi, Chori, Pa, Nirarchi and Nayaka (verb roots and agents). On earth: "bhavati: sah bhavatah, tau bhavanti, te" (present tense of the root bhu).
Bhavasi tvam, yuvam bhavathah, yuyam bhavatha, aham; bhavami, avam bhavavah, bhavamah — the lineage prospers (verb forms; edhate).
Edhete dve tatha edhante; edhase tvam hi medhaya; edhethe cha samedhadhve; edhe hi edhavahe dhiya (middle-voice present forms of edh).
